mainTopic: Do we worry that an עם הארץ will secretly swap food? Two challenges, from the innkeeper and from the women grinding grain, are each answered by showing a special motive in that case.
overview: Just before this, the גמרא explained that a mother-in-law is suspected of swapping food only because of a special motive. Now it asks whether we ever worry about swapping in general. It brings a משנה about an innkeeper suspected of swapping, and answers that she has a special motive: she wants the Torah student to eat her hot food. Next it brings a ברייתא about the wife of a חבר grinding grain with the wife of an עם הארץ, where רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says the עם הארץ's wife even hands out grain. The גמרא reasons that someone who steals would surely swap. רב יוסף answers that she too feels justified: 'the ox eats from its threshing.' The גמרא then turns to a story about רבי מאיר eating a vegetable leaf in בית שאן, which led רבי to permit all of בית שאן. When רבי's family objects that he is overturning their ancestors' practice, רבי begins his answer with the פסוק about חזקיהו breaking the copper snake. He asks why the righteous kings אסא and יהושפט had not already destroyed it, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Challenge from the innkeeper who swaps food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that we don't worry about swapping, using a משנה about an innkeeper who is suspected of swapping.
steps.simpleTranslation: In general, do we really not worry about swapping? But a משנה teaches: someone who gives food to his innkeeper must tithe what he gives her and what he takes back, because she is suspected of swapping!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether, apart from the mother-in-law case, we really never worry that someone will swap food. It quotes a משנה showing that we do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says an innkeeper who is an עם הארץ is suspected of swapping the food she cooks for you. That means you must tithe the food twice: before you give it and after you get it back. So it seems we do worry about swapping, even without the special mother-in-law motive.

keyTerms.meaning: we are concerned or worried about
an innkeeper (a woman who cooks or bakes for guests)
she swaps or switches (one food for another)

phrases.english: And in general, are we not concerned?
But didn't we learn in a mishna:
One who gives to his innkeeper
phrases.notes: He gives her his dough or pot of food to bake or cook. She is an עם הארץ.

phrases.english: tithes what he gives her
and what he takes back from her,
because she is suspected of swapping!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up from the earlier answer, which said the mother-in-law swaps only because of a special motive.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that, without a special motive, we don't worry that an עם הארץ will swap food.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה about the innkeeper shows a general suspicion of swapping, with no mother-in-law involved.

steps.title: The innkeeper also has a good motive
steps.stepSummary: The innkeeper swaps only because she tells herself the Torah student deserves her hot food.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, she justifies it and says: let the Torah student eat my hot food, and I will eat his cold food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the innkeeper is also a special case. She has a 'kind' reason to swap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She swaps because she wants to honor the Torah student with her fresh, hot food, while she eats his cold food. So the case still doesn't prove that people swap in general. They swap only when they can convince themselves it's a good deed.

keyTerms.meaning: she rules for herself, she justifies it (gives herself a 'permission')
a Torah student (literally, 'son of the house of the רב')

phrases.english: There too, she justifies it to herself and says:
Let the Torah student eat hot food,
and I will eat cold food.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the swap comes from a special good-hearted motive.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The innkeeper case shows a general suspicion of swapping.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even the innkeeper swaps only because she thinks she is honoring the Torah student, so there is no general suspicion.
steps.whatToRemember: The pattern: whenever a source shows an עם הארץ swapping, the גמרא explains it as a special case where the person feels justified.

steps.title: Challenge from the women grinding grain
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא limits when a חבר's wife may grind with an עם הארץ's wife, which suggests there is a worry about swapping.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really not worry about swapping? But a ברייתא teaches: the wife of a חבר may grind with the wife of an עם הארץ when she is impure, but not when she is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge from a ברייתא about two women grinding grain together. This opens a proof that the next steps will finish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the חבר's wife is impure, she won't touch or eat the grain, so there is no problem. When she is pure, she might eat the untithed grain, so she may not grind. The ברייתא shows there is real concern around the עם הארץ's grain, and the גמרא will sharpen this into a proof about swapping.

keyTerms.meaning: the wife of a חבר, someone careful about טומאה, טהרה and tithes
a person not careful about tithes and purity

phrases.english: And are we not concerned about swapping?
But isn't it taught in a baraita:
The wife of a ḥaver grinds
with the wife of an am ha'aretz
when she is impure,
phrases.notes: Since she is impure, she keeps her hands off the grain so she won't make it impure. So she won't eat any of it either.

phrases.english: but not when she is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge on the same point, after the first one was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that we don't worry about swapping in general.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats the עם הארץ's wife as untrustworthy around food. The next steps turn this into a proof that she would swap.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: the other woman gives her grain to eat
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר forbids grinding together even when impure, because the עם הארץ's wife hands her grain to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: even when she is impure she should not grind, because her companion gives her grain and she eats it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is still part of the same ברייתא. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר adds a stricter opinion, and the גמרא will build its question on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being impure doesn't help, because the חבר's wife doesn't need to touch the pile herself. The עם הארץ's wife simply hands her some grain to eat. That means the עם הארץ's wife gives away her husband's grain without permission.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף בִּזְמַן שֶׁהִיא טְמֵאָה לֹא תִּטְחוֹן,
phrases.english: Even when she is impure she should not grind,
because her companion gives her and she eats.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a stricter view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even an impure חבר's wife may not grind with an עם הארץ's wife, since she will be handed grain to eat.

steps.title: If she steals, surely she swaps
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues: if the עם הארץ's wife is willing to steal, she would certainly be willing to swap.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, if she even steals, do we need to ask whether she swaps?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge. It reasons from the bigger wrong to the smaller one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving away her husband's grain is actual stealing. Swapping is a smaller wrong than stealing. So if she is suspected of stealing, she must surely be suspected of swapping, which goes against the idea that we don't worry about swapping.

phrases.english: Now, she even steals,
phrases.notes: She hands out her husband's grain without his permission, as רבי שמעון בן אלעזר just said.

phrases.english: is swapping even a question?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the ברייתא brought in steps 3-4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that we don't worry about swapping.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone suspected of stealing is surely suspected of the smaller wrong of swapping.

steps.title: רב יוסף: she thinks the grinder deserves a share
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the עם הארץ's wife has a special excuse: whoever does the work gets to eat from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: there too she justifies it and says, 'the ox eats from its threshing.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the challenge the same way the innkeeper case was answered. The woman has a special reason that makes her feel it's allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She believes the חבר's wife, who is helping to grind, has earned a little of the grain, just like an ox may eat while threshing. So she doesn't see it as stealing. This tells us nothing about swapping in a normal case.

keyTerms.meaning: its threshing (the grain it is working on)

steps.whatToRemember: Both challenges fail for the same reason. The suspicion comes only when the עם הארץ has a reason to feel her act is justified, so in general we do not worry about swapping.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying she is honest. She still gives away the grain. The point is only that she does it because she feels justified, so it doesn't prove she would swap in an ordinary case.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
There too, she justifies it to herself and says,
"The ox eats from its threshing."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הָתָם נָמֵי מוֹרְיָא וְאָמְרָה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the act comes from a special self-justification.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since she steals, she would certainly swap.
steps.terutzMaskana: She gives the grain only because she believes the helper deserves a share, so this proves nothing about swapping in general.
steps.whyThisMatters: It confirms the rule that an עם הארץ is not generally suspected of swapping, which the earlier part of the sugya depends on.

steps.title: Testimony about רבי מאיר leads רבי to permit בית שאן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן זרוז testifies that רבי מאיר ate a vegetable leaf in בית שאן, and רבי permits all of בית שאן based on this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן זרוז, the son of רבי מאיר's father-in-law, testified before רבי that רבי מאיר ate a leaf of a vegetable in בית שאן. Based on this, רבי permitted all of בית שאן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story: a witness reports that רבי מאיר ate untithed produce in בית שאן, and רבי rules that all of בית שאן is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating there without separating מעשר shows that רבי מאיר held בית שאן does not have the holiness of ארץ ישראל for these laws. רבי trusted this and made it a general ruling for the whole city. This starts a new story, separate from the earlier discussion about the עם הארץ's wife.

keyTerms.meaning: A city on the edge of ארץ ישראל whose status for מעשר was in doubt

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Zeruz testified,
the son of Rabbi Meir's father-in-law,
before Rabbi about Rabbi Meir
phrases.notes: When the גמרא just says "רבי," it means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: that he ate a leaf of a vegetable
in Beit She'an,
phrases.notes: He ate it without separating תרומה or מעשר.

phrases.english: and Rabbi permitted Beit She'an
all of it, based on him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the swapping discussion and goes back to the earlier theme about רבי מאיר and the righteous, opening a new story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Based on testimony that רבי מאיר ate untithed produce there, רבי permitted all of בית שאן.

steps.title: The family objects to changing an old practice
steps.stepSummary: רבי's brothers and family protest that he is permitting what their ancestors treated as forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: His brothers and his father's household joined together against him and said: In a place where your fathers and grandfathers acted as if it was forbidden, will you act as if it is permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי's own family challenges his ruling, saying he should not overturn what earlier generations did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their attack is not about the facts of רבי מאיר's testimony. It is about tradition: if the ancestors kept בית שאן as forbidden, how can one person now permit it? This sets up the need for רבי to explain why an old practice can be changed.

keyTerms.meaning: they treated it as forbidden (as their practice)

phrases.english: His brothers and his father's household joined together against him,
they said to him:
A place where your fathers and your fathers' fathers
treated it as forbidden,
will you treat it as permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: חָבְרוּ עָלָיו אֶחָיו וּבֵית אָבִיו, אָמְרוּ לוֹ
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's decision to permit all of בית שאן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A practice kept as forbidden by many generations should not be overturned by a later authority.

steps.title: רבי begins his answer with the פסוק of the copper snake
steps.stepSummary: רבי quotes the פסוק saying חזקיהו broke the copper snake of משה because the people were burning incense to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He explained this פסוק to them: "And he broke the copper snake that משה made, for until those days the children of Israel were burning incense to it, and he called it נחשתן."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי starts answering his family by quoting a פסוק. This is a setup line: the next step builds on it, and his conclusion comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק shows that the copper snake was used for idol worship and was only destroyed in the days of חזקיהו. רבי will use this to show that earlier generations sometimes left something undone for a later leader to fix.

keyTerms.meaning: he expounded; explained the deeper meaning of a פסוק
the copper snake that משה made in the desert
a name for the snake, meaning a mere piece of copper

phrases.english: He expounded this verse to them:
"And he broke in pieces the copper snake
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 18:4. The one breaking it is King חזקיהו.

phrases.english: that Moshe had made,
for until those days
the children of Israel were burning incense to it,
and he called it Nechushtan."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי begins answering the family's objection from Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי begins his defense by bringing a פסוק showing an idol that lasted until חזקיהו destroyed it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precedent from a פסוק: earlier righteous leaders sometimes left something undone for a later leader to fix.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A practice kept as forbidden by earlier generations can never be overturned by a later authority.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even the copper snake stayed until חזקיהו removed it, so a later leader may change what earlier generations left in place. רבי continues this point in the next step and finishes it on the next amud.

steps.title: Why did אסא and יהושפט not destroy the snake?
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks how righteous kings like אסא and יהושפט, who destroyed all idol worship, could have left the copper snake standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it possible that אסא came and did not destroy it, and יהושפט came and did not destroy it? But אסא and יהושפט destroyed all the idol worship in the world!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי points out a puzzle in the פסוק: earlier righteous kings wiped out idol worship, so why was the snake still there? He is setting up the lesson he will draw next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since אסא and יהושפט surely could have destroyed the snake, it seems they deliberately left it. That suggests earlier leaders sometimes leave a task for a later leader. רבי will use this to justify his own new ruling about בית שאן.
steps.confusionAlert: This question is not challenging רבי's ruling. רבי himself is asking it as part of his answer, to lead into his main point.

phrases.english: Is it possible that Asa came and did not destroy it,
Yehoshafat came and did not destroy it?
But didn't all the idol worship in the world
Asa and Yehoshafat destroy!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a question about the פסוק quoted in Step 9 to build רבי's argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why righteous kings who destroyed all idol worship left the copper snake in place.
